name: Window Management (multi-screen)
plain: Asks to see all connected monitors and place windows on them.
meaning: Reveals how many screens you have, their sizes, positions, labels and scale. That is a strong device fingerprint and lets a site open fullscreen windows on a chosen monitor.

access.prompt_ui: Chrome prompt: Manage windows on all your displays, Allow or Block. screen.isExtended is readable without a prompt.
steps: Open or fullscreen on a chosen screen

chrome.note: Window Management API ships as window-placement in 100, renamed in 111

data.metric: ScreenDetails with one ScreenDetailed per monitor

limits.headline: Can see all your connected screens and place windows on them, if you allow
limits.user_action: You click Use all screens or Present on second monitor, then Allow.
can: List your screens with their size and position
Open windows on the screen you choose
Go fullscreen on a chosen monitor
Tell that more than one screen is attached, without asking you
cannot: List your screens before you click Allow
See your windows from other apps
limits.reach_label: While you use it, after Allow
limits.differs: Chrome and Edge on computers only. Firefox and Safari do not have it.

story.what_it_is: Asks to see all your connected monitors and place windows on them.

marketing.name: Window Management API
marketing.pitch: Chrome says it lets web apps see and use multiple screens, for example presentations across displays.

story.for_you: Your browser asks, 'Manage windows on all your displays?' If you say yes, the site can open its own windows on each screen, like speaker notes on one and slides on another.
story.for_makers: It lets web apps compete with desktop apps in setups with many screens. It also reveals your layout of monitors, so browsers ask first.

use_cases.example: A slide app puts the presentation on the projector and speaker notes on your laptop screen.
A browser flight or racing game opens a map, dashboard or chat on a second monitor.
A trading or operations dashboard opens charts across several monitors in one click.
A video or music editor in the browser puts the timeline on one screen and the preview on another.
A web control room for live events opens one window per camera on a wall of screens.
A security camera web page opens many feeds across a monitor wall.
A lecture tool shows slides to students and notes to the teacher.

technical_bounds: Fullscreen on chosen screen still needs a gesture

abuse: Placing fullscreen pages over other windows

history.change: Window Placement API ships as window-placement permission
Renamed Window Management, permission name window-management
